details: The cryptocurrency market experienced a significant downturn, with Bitcoin falling to approximately $63,500, its lowest level since August 2026, and Ethereum also seeing sharp declines. This selloff is driven by growing expectations of a December Federal Reserve rate hike, leading to a stronger US dollar and reduced appetite for risk assets. US spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded substantial net outflows, exceeding $2 billion in November, and over $1 billion in leveraged long positions were liquidated, further pressuring prices.
title: Crypto Market Sees Steep Declines; Bitcoin Below $64K, ETF Outflows Persist

details: JPMorgan Chase, despite its CEO's past skepticism towards crypto, has significantly increased its exposure to crypto-linked stocks and funds. Regulatory filings show the bank now holds close to $1 billion in assets across spot Bitcoin ETFs, Michael Saylor's Strategy, and crypto equity funds, deepening these positions in the third quarter.
title: JPMorgan Nears $1 Billion in Crypto-Linked Holdings

details: Pi Network (Pi) saw a notable 12% drop in 24 hours to $0.0611, underperforming the broader crypto market which was down 6.2%. The decline is primarily attributed to the overall market selloff, including expectations of a Fed rate cut and corporate selling. No specific Pi-related news or on-chain activity was identified as the sole cause for its steeper fall.
title: Pi Network Drops 12% as Wider Crypto Market Declines

details: Prediction market platform Kalshi is reportedly seeking new funding at a $65 billion valuation, a significant increase from its $40 billion Series G round. This move comes ahead of a potential future IPO, though Kalshi's CEO has stated an IPO is not planned for 2026. The platform faces regulatory opposition over gambling laws, despite the CFTC defending its jurisdiction.
title: Prediction Market Kalshi Seeks $65B Valuation Pre-IPO

details: OKXICE is set to launch its tokenized securities venue on November 23rd, operating under the SEC's five-year innovation exemption. The platform will initially offer over 70 tokenized securities, including shares of Strategy, Coinbase, and Circle. Trading will be restricted to eligible US customers who have completed identity checks, with tokens held in their own wallets.
title: OKXICE to Launch Tokenized Stock Trading Venue Nov 23
